articles.title: After red alert, Ganjam & Kandhamal gear up with control room, cyclone shelters - The Times of India
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Andaman and Nicobar Islands
articles.full_text:
Berhampur: In the wake of a red alert issued by the
India Meteorological Department (IMD) for extremely heavy rainfall likely on Sept 23 and 24 under the influence of a possible deep depression, Ganjam and Kandhamal districts have geared up to face any eventuality.
While the Ganjam administration has set up a control room and is reading cyclone shelters, besides asking fishermen not to venture into the sea, Kandhamal has planned to close a landslide-prone stretch at Kaling Ghat on National Highway-157 on Sept 23 and 24.
As a precautionary measure, the Ganjam district administration has asked its employees to remain at their workplaces, besides directing the fishermen who are in the deep sea to return to their native villages by Monday evening.
The administration has set up a control room at Chhatrapur to monitor the situation, while advising people not to venture outside during the rain.
Ganjam collector Keerthi Vasan V, during a meeting with the officials concerned, asked them to prepare for any eventuality. He directed the officials to prepare cyclone shelters in the district, so that the residents of the low-lying areas could be shifted there as a safety measure, if needed.
He has also asked the fishermen not to venture into the sea for fishing from Monday.
Devidutta Mohanty, assistant director of fisheries (marine), Ganjam, said they have raised awareness in fishermen-dominated villages since Sunday afternoon, following the collector's direction. "As reported, the fishermen have not gone to the sea on Monday,” he said.
He added they will submit a report on the safe berthing of the fishing boats, with a joint inspection by the tehsildar and fishery officials concerned. A total of 1,591 fishing boats are in the district in its three units: Gopalpur, Sunapur and Ganjam, he said.
Kandhamal collector Ved Bhusan said they have planned to close the landslide-prone stretch at Kaling Ghat on National Highway-157 on Sept 23 and 24, as a precautionary measure. The vehicular traffic will be diverted via Chakapada after it is closed, he said.
Last Sept too, the road, connecting Kandhamal and Ganjam districts, had been closed for several days due to massive landslides.

Maharashtra drought: Relief measures already initiated by state government, says CM Fadnavis
Maharashtra Chief Minister said formal crop-loss assessments, or panchnamas, would be carried out after October 5 as required under the rules. The findings would then be used to seek assistance from the Centre
CM Fadnavis said formal crop-loss assessments, or panchnamas, would be carried out after October 5. File Pic
Amid Opposition demands for an immediate drought declaration in Maharashtra, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Monday said the state government had already started implementing drought-relief measures and would not wait for assistance from the Centre to support farmers facing crop losses due to inadequate rainfall, reported the PTI.
Fadnavis said the state would provide assistance from its own funds while following the required procedure to seek financial support under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF).

articles.full_text:
Nanded, Sep 21: A 'yellow' alert for rain accompanied by thunderstorm and lightning has been issued for Nanded district in Maharashtra from September 21 to 24, an official said on Monday.
Citing the forecast by the India Meteorological Department's Regional Meteorological Centre in Mumbai, the official said there is likelihood of light to moderate rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kilometres per hour (kmph) at isolated places on September 21, 22 and 24.
On September 23, there is higher possibility of "heavy rainfall at isolated places", accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph, he added.
In view of the forecast, all concerned government agencies have been directed to take necessary precautionary and preventive measures, the official said.
District Disaster Management Officer Kishor Kunhe urged citizens to follow weather-related advisories and take necessary precautions during the alert period.
The administration advised people to avoid venturing outdoors during thunderstorms and lightning.
"Those caught in open areas should seek shelter in a safe building. If no safe shelter is available, they should move to a low-lying area and sit with their head between their knees. Citizens have also been advised not to remain on balconies, rooftops or open verandas during lightning activity," it said.
People should switch off electrical appliances and, where possible, disconnect their power supply during thunderstorms. They should stay away from wire fences, electric poles and other metal objects. Anyone in water should immediately move to a safe place, the administration said in its advisory.
"Avoid using landline phones, taking showers, touching taps or water pipelines and using electrical appliances during lightning activity. People should also avoid taking shelter in tents or sheds with metal frames, or standing under tall trees and near high metal towers," the administration said.
Citizens staying indoors have been advised not to stand near open doors or windows to watch lightning, it said, adding that people should avoid unnecessary travel and remain in safe places during the period of adverse weather.

Diesel relief measures face mixed fortunes
Federal lawmakers have aimed a number of proposals at fuel and the increasing costs.
Some have gained traction while others have not.
As of Monday, Sept. 21, AAA reported a national average diesel price of $6.51 per gallon. The highest price ever recorded by the organization.
A recent push by House Republicans to suspend the federal fuel tax in hopes of lowering current fuel prices has fallen apart.
Reports indicate that a major sticking point in the process was concerns within the House that the Highway Trust Fund would be depleted, while others have called it a stunt.
Edward J. Markey, ranking member of the U.S. Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship, called for an end to the war with Iran, saying American families are facing an increase of more than $1,400 in fuel costs.
“American service members are paying the ultimate price abroad as Americans at home are struggling to afford gas, groceries, and healthcare,” Markey said.
Fuel waiver
On Wednesday, Sept. 16, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration granted hours-of-service relief for truck drivers transporting fuel.
Drivers covered by this order can operate for up to 16 hours within a 24-hour window, as long as they take required rest breaks.
FMCSA said global supply disruptions, anticipated increases in demand in the near future and mitigating impacts on the cost and availability of fuel are what led the agency to declare the emergency.
This waiver will remain in effect through Dec. 16.
Cold weather measures
On Wednesday, Sept. 16, the Cold Weather Diesel Reliability Act, introduced in November 2025, was advanced by the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee.
The bill would provide year-round exemptions from DEF system requirements for vehicles and equipment that operate primarily in cold climates, such as Alaska and Wyoming.
“When a truck or piece of heavy equipment is forced by EPA mandates to shut down in extreme cold because of a faulty sensor not made for the cold, it’s not just an inconvenience—it can quickly become a life-threatening situation,” Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, said. “The Cold Weather Diesel Reliability Act will bring common sense to EPA rules and ensure that trucks and heavy equipment can continue operating safely and reliably in the nation’s coldest regions.” LL
